title_prefix: Miniscript parsing and inference are cub
mechanism: make-ms-node computes script-size as (length (ms-node-script node)) (src/validation/miniscript.lisp:589) and ms-node-script re-serializes the WHOLE subtree from scratch each time; make-ms-node runs once per node, so total work is the sum over i of O(i^2) = O(n^3) in the size of the expression. ms-parse carries no running size bound and imposes no length limit on its input, and ms-from-script does not refuse an oversized script before decomposing it -- the only ceiling is the per-step ms-node-valid-p bail inside the decode loop (:1785), which is reached only after the cubic work up to that point has been paid. Core bounds this twice: Node::CalcScriptLen / ComputeScriptLen derives a node's length in O(1) from its fragment, its first sub's type and the sum of its subs' lengths and caches it in the constructor (refs/bitcoin/src/script/miniscript.cpp:265-296), and Parse's running script_size returns {} as soon as it exceeds MaxScriptSize (miniscript.h:1912, re-checked per wrapper character at :1931), with FromScript refusing an over-size script before decomposing it (:2692).
consequence: One authenticated RPC request burns minutes of CPU in one RPC worker, and the worker pool is bounded by -rpcthreads (src/rpc/server.lisp:1416-1424, Core's default 16), so a handful of concurrent requests exhausts the JSON-RPC surface of the node. Every descriptor-parsing RPC is a vector (getdescriptorinfo, deriveaddresses, importdescriptors, scantxoutset) and so is every witnessScript-inference path (signrawtransactionwithkey and walletprocesspsbt via src/rpc/rawtransaction.lisp:469, wallet coin sizing via src/wallet/wallet-spend.lisp:489). There is no earlier length cap: parse-descriptor (src/rpc/descriptors.lisp:1032) does not bound the string, and the only limit above it is +max-rpc-body-size+ = 0x02000000 (32 MiB) at src/rpc/server.lisp:692, which is not a meaningful bound. Notably the witnessScript vector needs no oversized input at all -- a 3600-byte witnessScript is WITHIN the standardness limit and already costs 37 s.
evidence: Container: /Users/sen/common-lisp/bl-ga11v-miniscript-s2, warm image, DEV_EVAL_TIMEOUT=900, build/ga11probe/p3.lisp and p3b.lisp; wall clock taken inside the image with get-internal-real-time. Input: 'n:' repeated N times followed by '1'. ms-parse, :p2wsh -- N=500 (1001 chars) 151 ms; N=2000 (4001 chars) 6402 ms; N=5000 (10001 chars) 98770 ms, and that last verdict is INVALID (script-size 5001 > 3600), i.e. 98.8 seconds spent to reach a conclusion Core reaches after 3600 accumulated bytes. The 4001->10001 step is 2.5x input for 15.4x time against a cubic prediction of 15.6x. ms-from-script over OP_1 followed by N OP_0NOTEQUAL -- 501 bytes 121 ms; 2001 bytes 6599 ms; 3601 bytes 37275 ms (returning NIL). Through the shipped RPC dispatcher: bl.rpc:dispatch-rpc-method 'getdescriptorinfo' with wsh(n:n:...1), 10015 characters including the checksum, took 97671 ms in one call before raising RPC error -5; bl.rpc:dispatch-rpc-method 'signrawtransactionwithkey' with a caller-supplied 3600-byte witnessScript in prevtxs took 36987 ms and returned complete:false. Confirmed absence of an earlier cap by grep over src/rpc/descriptors.lisp (no length test on the descriptor string) and src/rpc/server.lisp:692/1069/1092.
fix_shape: The bound and the cost are one fix. Port Core's running script_size into ms-parse (seeded at 1, incremented per fragment and per wrapper character by the constants at miniscript.h:1960-2090 and :1931) and test it against ms-max-script-size at the top of the parse loop, failing the parse immediately -- that alone caps the work at 3600 bytes of accumulated script for P2WSH. Independently, replace make-ms-node's (length (ms-node-script node)) with Core's ComputeScriptLen (miniscript.cpp:265-296), an O(1) function of the fragment, the first sub's type and the sum of the subs' cached lengths, which removes the quadratic-per-node re-serialization and makes the whole parse linear. For the inference direction add Core's FromScript pre-check (miniscript.h:2692): refuse a script larger than MaxScriptSize before decomposing it. Both halves also close 05af23cd, since a shape-derived size needs no key bytes. Re-test node_deep_destruct-style stack safety (refs/bitcoin/src/test/miniscript_tests.cpp:730) together with this change: our tree walks are plain recursion where Core's are explicit stacks, and the cubic cost is currently what makes a deep tree unreachable.
